label: rem:organic-chain-taxonomy
title: Organic chain taxonomy from bond-order patterns
html:
The molecular Hopf chain framework generates the standard classes of organic molecules by varying the bond-order pattern and whether the chain is open or closed.

Bond-order classification.

Class Bond-order pattern Free sites per C Hydrogen capacity
Alkane (saturated) (1, 1, \ldots, 1) 2 (interior), 3 (endpoint) 2N + 2 (chain), 2N (ring)
Alkene (\ldots, 2, \ldots) 1 at double bond 2N (one double bond)
Alkyne (\ldots, 3, \ldots) 0 at triple bond 2N - 2 (one triple bond)
Cumulene (2, 2, \ldots, 2) 0 (interior), 2 (endpoint) 4
Polyyne (1, 3, 1, 3, \ldots) 0 (interior) 2

Saturation as linking-site occupancy. Raising the bond order by one unit consumes one free linking site on each adjacent carbon. Saturation is the extreme case where every backbone bond is single.

Open vs. closed (chain vs. ring). Whether the backbone closes into a ring shifts the hydrogen count by a fixed offset. The total degree of unsaturation is d = \sum_i (k_i - 1).

Aromatic rings. A closed ring with d = N/2 is aromatic. The secondary Hopf ring formed by extra trefoils is closed. We conjecture that Hückel's 4n + 2 rule corresponds to a sub-Hopf link closure condition.
